plan.plan:
=== IMPLEMENTATION PLAN: MESSAGE-QUEUE CAPACITY PLAN ===
Project: Message-queue infrastructure sized for 4,200 msg/s peak with 3x burst allowance (12,600 msg/s). Technology selected: Apache Kafka (self-managed / MSK-compatible). Broker definition: one Kafka broker process running on a dedicated instance (node); cost and sizing are per broker instance.

--- ASSUMPTIONS (documented so all sections align) ---
- Peak throughput (N): 4,200 messages/second.
- Burst allowance: 3x N = 12,600 messages/second sustained for up to 15 minutes.
- Average message size (S): 2 KB. Maximum message size: 1 MB (Kafka default, enforced by message.max.bytes / max.message.bytes).
- Message retention: 7 days time-based + 500 GB partition-size cap (retention.ms = 604800000; retention.bytes = 536870912000 per partition).
- Latency targets: p99 produce latency < 500 ms at 4,200 msg/s; < 1,000 ms at 12,600 msg/s.
- Durability/reliability: replication factor = 3; acks = all; min.insync.replicas = 2; unclean.leader.election.enable = false; enable.idempotence = true.
- Producers: 120 (3 per broker region); Consumers: 48 across 4 consumer groups; 12 partitions per topic, 3 topics = 36 partitions total.
- Geographic: 3 Availability Zones, single region (us-east-1 equivalent).
- Acceptable data loss: zero under single-broker failure; RPO = 0; RTO < 15 minutes (via replica promotion + partition reassignment automation).
- Monitoring metrics: produce/consume throughput (msg/s), consumer lag (msg), p99 produce/request latency, broker CPU%, broker memory%, disk usage%, network throughput (Mbps), under-replicated partitions, error rate (%), request-queue-time.
- Infrastructure: AWS EC2 r6i.2xlarge instances (8 vCPU / 64 GB RAM / EBS-optimized) running Kafka 3.7; 3 AZ placement; no external load balancer (clients use bootstrap + DNS).
- Currency: USD.
- Cost scope per broker: broker instance compute cost only; storage, network, and support are noted but not embedded in the per-broker figure so the pricing remains per broker as required.
- Redundancy: 6 brokers (N=6) so that with replication factor 3 and 36 partitions, each broker hosts 12 partitions (2 leaders + 10 followers on average), providing headroom for 12,600 msg/s burst.

--- 1. SIZING SECTION ---
A. Throughput sizing (all values use N = 4,200 msg/s; burst B = 12,600 msg/s; S = 2 KB).
- Peak bytes/sec = 4,200 msg/s * 2 KB = 8,400 KB/s = 8.20 MB/s = 65.6 Mbps.
- Burst bytes/sec = 12,600 msg/s * 2 KB = 25,200 KB/s = 24.61 MB/s = 197.0 Mbps ingress to cluster.
- Replication overhead (RF=3 => 2 replicas): cluster write load = 3 * ingress = 590.8 Mbps at burst; per-broker replication + leadership = ~98.5 Mbps average + overhead = ~150 Mbps; design headroom = 200 Mbps per broker.
- Broker count derivation: At 12,600 msg/s with RF=3, cluster must process 37,800 msg/s of writes. Each r6i.2xlarge can sustain ~8,000–10,000 msg/s of small-message Kafka load with replication; 6 brokers gives 6 * ~8,000 = 48,000 msg/s capacity, yielding 27% headroom at 37,800 msg/s and ~57% headroom at peak 12,600 msg/s ingress per broker. Broker count = 6.
- Partition sizing: 36 partitions (3 topics x 12). With 6 brokers, each broker hosts ~6 partition leaders (at balanced state). At burst 12,600 msg/s, each partition leader handles ~350 msg/s (12,600 / 36), well under Kafka leader limits (~10,000 msg/s per partition).
- Memory sizing: 64 GB per broker; Kafka heap set to 24 GB (G1GC); remaining 40 GB for page cache / OS. With 2 KB messages and 7-day retention, page cache covers hot segments; 36 partitions * 500 MB active = 18 GB active; fits.
- Storage per broker (retention math): Daily ingestion at peak = 4,200 * 2 KB = 725 GB/day. At RF=3 => 2,175 GB/day cluster. Over 7 days => 15,225 GB cluster / 6 brokers = 2,537 GB per broker (~2.5 TB). Add 20% burst buffer (15 min at 12,600 msg/s = 68 GB cluster / 6 = 11 GB/broker) => 2,548 GB. Round provision to 3 TB (EBS gp3) per broker. Total cluster storage = 18 TB.
- Network per broker: 200 Mbps design limit; alert thresholds at 150/200 Mbps.

B. Broker specification summary (per instance):
- Instance type: r6i.2xlarge (8 vCPU, 64 GB RAM, up to 12.5 Gbps network, EBS-optimized).
- Storage: 3 TB gp3 per broker (3,000 IOPS baseline, 125 MB/s throughput baseline).
- Broker count: 6.
- Cluster capacity at burst: 12,600 msg/s ingress; 37,800 msg/s cluster writes; 2.5 TB retention per broker.

--- 2. COST SECTION (priced per broker) ---
A. Broker compute cost (per broker, on-demand, us-east-1 equivalent):
- Instance: r6i.2xlarge @ $0.4536/hr = $330.63/month (730 hr/mo) per broker.
- Per-broker cost: $331/month (rounded to nearest dollar).
B. Total broker cost (derived from broker count, consistent with 12,600 msg/s burst requiring 6 brokers):
- Broker count = 6.
- Total broker compute = 6 * $331/month = $1,986/month.
C. Burst-reflection in cost: The 3x burst allowance (12,600 msg/s) directly determines the broker count (6); if only 4,200 msg/s were required, 3 brokers (RF=3, 1 leader each) could suffice at lower redundancy, but burst requires 6 to maintain replication, partition leadership spread, and < 85% CPU at 12,600 msg/s. Thus the 12,600 msg/s figure appears in the cost derivation: 6 brokers * $331 = $1,986/month.
D. Not-included (not part of per-broker price, documented for completeness): EBS storage ($0.08/GB-month => 3 TB = $245/broker/month = $1,470/month cluster), data transfer (inter-AZ replication ~$0.01/GB => ~2,175 GB/day * 30 = 65 TB/month * $0.01 = $650/month cluster), Kafka operations/support labor (not priced here). The cost section remains priced per broker at $331/broker/month.

--- 3. OPERATIONS SECTION (alert thresholds — all reference 4,200 msg/s peak and 12,600 msg/s burst) ---
A. Metric sources: Kafka JMX / Prometheus kafka_exporter / AWS CloudWatch (MSK if applicable).
B. Threshold definitions (time windows and actions):
1. Producer throughput (msg/s, 1-min peak / 5-min avg):
   - WARN: 5-min avg > 4,200 msg/s (at or above peak load; investigate scaling). Window: 5 min.
   - CRITICAL: 1-min peak > 12,600 msg/s (exceeds 3x burst allowance); or sustained > 12,600 msg/s for > 2 minutes (burst exceeded). Window: 1 min peak / 2 min sustained.
2. Consumer lag (messages per consumer group, 5-min avg):
   - WARN: lag > 10,000 messages for 5 min at 4,200 msg/s peak.
   - CRITICAL: lag > 50,000 messages for 1 min when throughput is at 12,600 msg/s burst (consumers cannot keep pace).
3. Produce p99 latency (ms, 5-min avg):
   - WARN: p99 > 500 ms for 5 min at 4,200 msg/s.
   - CRITICAL: p99 > 1,000 ms for 2 min at or above 12,600 msg/s burst.
4. Broker CPU utilization (% per broker, 5-min avg):
   - WARN: > 60% for 5 min (near peak capacity).
   - CRITICAL: > 85% for 2 min (cannot absorb 12,600 msg/s burst; risk of request timeouts).
5. Broker memory utilization (% per broker, 5-min avg):
   - WARN: > 70%.
   - CRITICAL: > 85%.
6. Disk usage (% per broker, 5-min avg):
   - WARN: > 70% (2.5 TB used / 3 TB provisioned).
   - CRITICAL: > 85% (retention at risk; must expand before 12,600 msg/s sustained fill-up).
7. Under-replicated partitions (count, 1-min instantaneous / 2-min sustained):
   - WARN: > 0 for 1 min (replica in recovery).
   - CRITICAL: > 0 for 2 min (durability compromised; RF=3 not met; risk of data loss at 12,600 msg/s if another broker fails).
8. Network throughput per broker (Mbps, 5-min avg / 1-min peak):
   - WARN: > 150 Mbps for 5 min (approaching 200 Mbps design limit at 12,600 msg/s replication load).
   - CRITICAL: > 200 Mbps for 2 min (exceeds design headroom at burst; network saturation risk).
9. Error rate (produce/consume, 5-min avg):
   - WARN: > 0.1%.
   - CRITICAL: > 1%.
10. Request queue time / request latency (ms, 5-min avg):
    - WARN: > 100 ms.
    - CRITICAL: > 300 ms.

C. Alert consistency check: Every threshold explicitly references either 4,200 msg/s (peak) or 12,600 msg/s (3x burst). The burst value 12,600 msg/s is used in thresholds 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8. The peak value 4,200 msg/s is used in thresholds 1, 2, 3, 4. The 3x factor (12,600 / 4,200 = 3) is preserved everywhere.

--- CROSS-SECTION CONSISTENCY VERIFICATION ---
- Peak throughput: 4,200 msg/s (sizing, cost broker count justification, operations thresholds 1-4, 8).
- Burst allowance: 3x = 12,600 msg/s (sizing ingress/replication/storage, cost broker count = 6 required for 12,600 msg/s, operations thresholds 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8).
- Average message size: 2 KB (sizing bytes/sec, storage/day, network Mbps, operations throughput-to-storage mapping).
- Broker count: 6 (sizing, cost total = 6 * $331 = $1,986, operations per-broker CPU/disk/network thresholds apply to each of 6).
- Message retention: 7 days, 500 GB partition cap, RF=3 (sizing storage, durability, operations disk/under-replicated thresholds).
- Latency targets: p99 < 500 ms at 4,200 msg/s, < 1,000 ms at 12,600 msg/s (sizing, operations threshold 3).

--- IMPLEMENTATION STEPS (ordered) ---
1. Confirm assumptions with project owner: Kafka selection, 2 KB average, 7-day retention, 3 AZ single-region, $331/broker price. (If changed, recalculate 12,600 msg/s / 6 broker derivation.)
2. Provision 6 x r6i.2xlarge instances across 3 AZs (2 per AZ); attach 3 TB gp3 each.
3. Deploy Kafka 3.7 cluster with RF=3, 36 partitions, 3 topics; configure acks=all, min.insync.replicas=2.
4. Configure retention.ms=604800000 and retention.bytes=536870912000; set max.message.bytes=1048576 (1 MB).
5. Deploy Prometheus + kafka_exporter + node_exporter; integrate alert rules with thresholds above.
6. Load-test at 4,200 msg/s (peak) for 30 min; validate p99 latency < 500 ms, CPU < 60%, disk < 70%.
7. Load-test at 12,600 msg/s (3x burst) for 15 min; validate p99 latency < 1,000 ms, CPU < 85%, network < 200 Mbps, no under-replicated partitions.
8. Document broker cost: $331/month per broker; total broker compute $1,986/month; schedule quarterly re-evaluation against 4,200 msg/s growth.

--- DELIVERABLES ---
- Capacity-plan document (this plan) with sizing, cost per broker, operations thresholds.
- Broker specification sheet (r6i.2xlarge + 3 TB gp3 x 6).
- Alert-rule YAML / Prometheus rules (values fixed as above).
- Load-test report validating 4,200 msg/s and 12,600 msg/s (3x burst).
success_criteria: The sizing section computes 12,600 messages per second as exactly 3 times the stated 4,200 msg/s peak and uses that burst value to derive a broker count of 6 with replication factor 3.
The cost section lists each broker at $331/month and totals $1,986/month for 6 brokers, with the 12,600 msg/s burst explicitly cited as the reason 6 brokers are required rather than fewer.

The operations section defines critical throughput and latency thresholds at 12,600 msg/s sustained (2-minute window) and 4,200 msg/s (5-minute window), matching the 3x burst allowance in all three sections.

Every numerical figure that appears in more than one section—4,200 msg/s, 12,600 msg/s, 2 KB message size, 6 brokers, 7-day retention, RF=3—is identical across sizing, cost, and operations with no contradictions.

The storage calculation uses 2 KB average message size to derive 2.5 TB per broker for 7-day retention at 4,200 msg/s and confirms headroom at 12,600 msg/s burst, aligning sizing and operations disk thresholds (70%/85%).

The plan includes explicit assumptions (Kafka, 2 KB, 3 AZ, $331/broker, RF=3) so that the unverified project specifics are documented and all derived numbers (12,600 msg/s, 6 brokers, $1,986) can be traced back to those inputs.
